record_notes.DCP-LETT-1833: February 26,1856; four full body blocks, eight footnotes, annotations, bibliography and raw Greek/variant markup read. Proposed Bombay mail and probable same steamer as February23 are expectations, not actual Darwin receipt. Museum project and curatorship threat are future possibilities; Blyth allegations against medical rivals are not verified findings. Atkinson letter portion said enclosed is unpreserved. Two-week assistant illness is the reported present obstacle;1865 museum and later pay are editorial future. Panther/leopard etymology offered as Blyth interpretation, not externally established. Raw Harting Leopard and [var] near Panthera/Varia need supported source treatment, not silent guessed restoration. Greek panther word remains actual text. Quoted Chinese Repository artificial duck incubation distinct from Blyth speculation that ancient Egyptian practice concerned geese; current Egyptian fowl incubation stated separately. Darwin marginal Nothing for me except hatching eggs is undated, not a reply or instruction to our project.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1845: Undated thirteen-page signed memorandum, circa March22,1856. Seven retained body blocks, all thirty-two notes, bibliography, annotations, actual musk-ox sketch and two MathML halves read. P4 March22 separates earlier composition; ending implies completion later. Single XML day does not make all sections exactly March22. Explicit Darwin top annotation Received May6/56 is receipt evidence, separate from composition, reading completion and sequence13. Annobon fowl claim questioned after reading French article; purported French quotation is not exact published wording according to apparatus. Proceedings batch just received by Blyth, not Darwin. Owen musk-ox naming criticised with sketch drawn from memory of a printed portrait, not a live sighting. Pigeon varieties acquired by Blyth, sending and breeding/crossing still intended. Historic origin inferred from rump colour/names/textual absence, not proven. P3 half-way feathering and P4 half-dozen repetitions are genuine MathML, not12. Four attempted esplanade observations yielded no flock, so dark-feet contrast explicitly deferred. P5 now prefers African wild-ass origin, revising earlier Arabian emphasis; newly prepared paper later published1859 is not necessarily the same final version available to Darwin in1856. P7 is quoted March13 newspaper claim with Blyth comment, not independent survey or new Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1849: Undated eight-page memorandum, supplied April3,1856 solely from Darwin pencil annotation; distinguish this from an explicit receipt label. All twenty-one retained blocks, eight notes, bibliography, separate annotations and raw opening layout read. P1 Notes heading not letter prose for future content. P2 identifies David Scott manuscript copy, difficult left-handed writing after injury. P3–20 interleave Scott quotation and Blyth inserted observations; neither is Darwin voice. English/Hindustani list is broken into raw paragraphs with literal diag/ramme tokens and no table/image; matching may need manuscript layout, especially Gahu and unknown/illegible names. P15 two literal Unicode halves are already correct, not MathML. P3 now personally reports wild pigeons have pink feet, updating1845 deferred dark-foot conjecture; typical-coloured bald-pates also obtained, revising earlier limitation. Scott reports from Hansi and has not been stationed at Delhi/Lucknow; not universal coverage of those cities. Blyth finds local carriers better than Scott description and distinguishes differently patterned breeds despite naming overlap. P21 all domestic pigeons from livia/intermedia is expressly his judgment based on voice/pairing, and guinea-fowl historical trade continuity is his inference from Browne, not independent proof. Proposed foreign correspondents/procurement remain requests. Docket14 and other Darwin comparative notes are separate undated layer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1817: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 8, original header 1855 editorially corrected to 1856; all seventeen body blocks, sixty-eight footnotes, full long thirteen-section Notes for Mr Darwin enclosure, separate annotations and bibliography read. Corrected year supported by sequence and contents, not an arrival timestamp. Answers missing November 5 and 22 Darwin letters; Moore queries said to be separately forwarded are not preserved. Orang paper unavailable for this mail, lion paper available and ass paper referred to London publisher: these are different transmission states. P3 corrects misunderstanding: interbreeding within Coracias and within Treron, not between those genera. Railway anecdote source recalled uncertainly, camel parentage is reported and not automatically proved by one-humped appearance. Indian donkey stripes expressly not zebra intermixture. P8 onward are substantive postscripts after signature, including regional intergradation, species-versus-race uncertainty, isolated Mydaus populations and speculative cabbage origin. Historical racial and ethnographic assertions remain Blyth claims. Full enclosure contains nested quotations, guinea-fowl historical-origin arguments, contradictory flight observations, possible hare/grouse varieties, suspected pheasant relations, cattle notice and Crump forwarding lead, revised Turkey-name etymology and poultry-source inquiries. Two physically attached feathers described in footnote 44 are not pictured in current HTML; their markings are not independently visually verified. Later Origin/Variation/Natural selection citations and Darwin marginal abstracts do not date contemporary knowledge. Docket 10 is sequence numbering, not receipt. Enclosure is present in this HTML despite historical separate1818 label; do not count it twice. Separate Crump1819 is being recovered additively, not claimed read here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1825: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 23, 1856 exact Calcutta ALS; seven full blocks, thirty-one footnotes, annotations, bibliography and actual spur drawing read. Home letters arrived about midnight last night, including an undated Darwin letter whose postscript acknowledged October 8 and 22 Blyth letters. This provides indirect prior knowledge evidence but no surviving Darwin reply text or exact Darwin receipt day. Echo du monde savant known only through a cited review, not directly read by Blyth. Goldfish origin is a hypothesis; article and jungle-fowl skins are promised, not Darwin receipts. Blyth proposes five distinct gallinaceous families and corrects turkey tuft to feathers, while muscular foundation was news from Darwin. Live wild dog personally seen yesterday; putative later London transfer is prospective. Seychelles conspectus unknown, sources and specimens requested. P5 corrects numerous African fowls versus numerous races, and Rock Pigeons ambiguity; illustration shows extra spur arising beneath an existing spur, no scales or measurements. Bantam name versus biological origin and fallow-deer colour versus other variation kept distinct. Annotated number11 is not a delivery date. Bibliography Thomson1848 Lochaber entry does not match Allen and Thomson1848 Niger narrative cited in apparatus; do not use mismatched bibliography to replace source identity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1832: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. February 23, 1856 exact Calcutta ALS; five complete blocks, twenty-four footnotes, annotations, bibliography, raw half MathML and actual labelled Gallus head drawing read. Previous brief letter got to post office, not evidence it reached Darwin. Four printed appeal copies now sent versus rough proof sent previous mail; their exact identification as salary memorial is apparatus inference and eventual1864 pension is later. February20 anniversary walk is an actual prior event, proposed Calcutta gardens future. Gallus varius first living observation includes a pale bluish-lake comb, red/yellow throat regions and blue tip labelled in figure; hybrid Gallus oeneus claim remains Blyth report. Pigeon procurement and ten-pound proposal, macaw/marmoset barter and prices remain negotiations, not completed shipments. Complaint about Bartlett is Blyth allegation, no independent finding. P3 explicitly answers missing December16 Darwin letter, cannot recall exact authority for Oman asses or red-deer infertility. Wild dog is now dead with skin/skeleton preparation ongoing; earlier identification revised after Hodgson examination. Canine-hybrid experiment advocates matched sibling controls, not completed comparative results. P4 half-bred Sonneratii is 1/2, not twelve birds; observed repeated infertile eggs qualified by possible individual fertility differences. Coracias skins procured by Blyth, not Darwin. Northern/southern bird comparisons and tropical gaps qualified; Darwin consultation note is undated. Docket12 is sequence marker only.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Actually viewed left-facing low-headed shaggy bovine profile, rounded heavy torso, short tail and legs on a ground line. No labels or scale. Body explicitly says drawn from memory of an Arctic navigator’s portrait, with possibly still lower head, so do not treat as an observed or measured specimen.

Actually viewed black sketch of a bird foot and shank with projecting spurs. Extra projection lies below the base of another as described in P5; dotted stroke is visible. No caption, dimensions or quantitative scale.

Actually viewed side profile of a fowl head with large unserrated oval comb marked a, throat regions b/c and lower tip d. Visible legend reads a pale bluish-lake, b Red, c Bright yellow, d Blue. Black reproduction gives labelled colours rather than a colour photograph; no scale inferred.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
